training_data.name: Med-MathInstruct
training_data.quote: Dataset: Med-MathInstruct (MedInstruct combined from BioInstruct and AlpaCare-MedInstruct-52k, plus MQR data from MedCalc-Bench-v1.0). The training notebook loads combined_medical_math_train.jsonl, which has 61,375 rows, and combined_medical_math_val.jsonl, which has 3,409 rows.

training_data.name: MedCalc-Bench-v1.0
training_data.quote: The model card says the added portion is 15% MQR data from MedCalc-Bench-v1.0. The Hub dataset ncbi/MedCalc-Bench says it has 10,543 training instances of a patient note, a calculation question, an answer, and an explanation. The thesis sample file labels rows Subset: MedCalc_Bench. This checkpoint's train file is 8,005 rows larger than the MedInstruct-only train file, not the full 10,543.

training_data.name: BioInstruct
training_data.quote: BioInstruct is a dataset of 25k instructions and demonstrations generated by OpenAI's GPT-4 engine in July 2023.

training_data.name: AlpaCare-MedInstruct-52k
training_data.quote: The dataset README lists a train split of 52,002 examples. It does not say whether the text is human or model-written.

training_method.update_scope_quote: full fine-tuning trains all model parameters so requires_grad is set to true for all of them

description.text: Full fine-tuned LLaMA-3.2-3B-Instruct on medical instruction datasets plus 15% MQR data from MedCalc-Bench-v1.0 to improve medical quantitative reasoning.

output_type.quote: Type: Text generation / Instruction fine-tuned language model

use_claim.quote: Full fine-tuned LLaMA-3.2-3B-Instruct on medical instruction datasets plus 15% MQR data from MedCalc-Bench-v1.0 to improve medical quantitative reasoning.

quotes: Files from my master's thesis at UCOL. I fine-tuned LLaMA-3.2-3B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct on medical datasets using LoRA and full instruction tuning to investigate whether smaller models could improve at medical quantitative reasoning.

Solve the following clinical calculation. Extract the necessary variables from the patient note, show the step-by-step reasoning and formula used, and provide the final numeric result.
plus 15% MQR data from MedCalc-Bench-v1.0 to improve medical quantitative reasoning.
Evaluated all fine-tuned variants and base models across MedCalc-Bench-v1.0, MedQA-USMLE-4-options, and a custom MedInstruct test set. eval only

serving.text_only_input_quote: A MedCalc row in the thesis sample file is a text patient note plus a question, for example: What is the patient's CHA2DS2-VASc Score?
serving.notes: The training notebook sets an empty system prompt, loads the base in bfloat16, and uses the same schedule as the medical-only full tune: 3 epochs, learning rate 2e-5, per_device_train_batch_size 8, gradient_accumulation_steps 4. The card lists PEFT 0.18.1; this notebook uses Trainer and does not import PEFT. tokenizer_config.json has no chat_template key. Hub API safetensors total is 3212749824. The notebook saves medical-math_llama3_full_model and does not print this Hub id. No paper names this repository.

evaluation_reported.text: The thesis README says the added MedCalc data improved MedCalc-Bench-v1.0 across variants and had little effect on the other benchmarks. It does not give this file's MedCalc score alone. A result file for the local checkpoint medical-math_llama3_full_model reports MedQA 4-options accuracy 0.416 on 1,273 samples.

discrepancies: The inventory name Med-MathInstruct matches the card. It is not a Hub dataset id. The card says it is MedInstruct plus 15% MedCalc-Bench-v1.0 data. The card lists PEFT 0.18.1; the linked notebook trains all parameters with Trainer.
